🔥 The fire settles. the woman in her 40s, with restless hands has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "A monitor lizard the size of a canoe, light sliding wrong off its back — I put it down today." "It goes perfectly still and arches its back to the sun. The mirror-scales catch the light — the glare builds, builds — then it launches, blind-fast, straight at where you were standing." "The thick tail lifts off the ground, swaying once — then sweeps like a felled tree. A monitor's tail is a battering ram with scales." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Violet

EUREKA — the biggest burst so far." "It flickers — a smaller, meaner idea. Less certain, faster." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Moise mutters "And you're still standing." Diana says quietly "So it bleeds." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Diana mutters "Tell me you didn't go alone." Lucas says quietly "And you're still standing." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

"'Oh, it's TRYING again!' Double shame — it smells blood." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Diana breathes "And you're still standing." Hannah says quietly "The fire feels smaller now." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"
